subject: surgery
title: Stomach and duodenum: high-yield surgical essentials

steps.tx: Peptic ulcer disease is the commonest cause of upper GI bleeding. **Duodenal ulcers** are most often found in the first part of the duodenum. Most duodenal and gastric ulcers are linked to **Helicobacter pylori** infection, while NSAIDs are the other major cause. Endoscopy is the investigation of choice for diagnosis and bleeding control.

vis.alt: Diagram illustrating the distinct surgical complications of duodenal ulcers: anterior ulcers perforate into the peritoneum, while posterior ulcers erode into the gastroduodenal artery causing bleeding.
vis.caption: Anterior duodenal ulcers perforate; posterior ulcers erode into gastroduodenal artery

steps.tx: A perforated peptic ulcer causes sudden, severe generalised abdominal pain. The abdomen becomes board-like and rigid, and the patient avoids movement. Anterior ulcers tend to perforate, while posterior ulcers tend to bleed by eroding into the **gastroduodenal artery**, which is the vessel to ligate. Perforation needs prompt surgery to prevent septic peritonitis.

steps.tx: Gastric outlet obstruction causes repeated vomiting, which loses **hydrochloric acid** and **potassium**, producing **hypokalaemic hypochloraemic alkalosis**. The kidneys try to conserve sodium and excrete **hydrogen ions**, so urine can paradoxically be acidic. Restore circulating volume and correct the chloride and potassium deficits before operating, because a depleted patient tolerates anaesthesia and surgery poorly.

The kidneys try to conserve sodium and excrete hydrogen ions, so the urine can paradoxically be acidic. steps.tx: Surgery for duodenal ulcer has moved toward acid reduction and drainage. **Vagotomy and antrectomy** gives the lowest recurrence rate, and is also used for complicated ulcers. Post-vagotomy **diarrhoea** is the most common complication after truncal vagotomy. Gastrojejunostomy drains the stomach, and dumping syndrome can follow it or a gastrectomy.

steps.tx: Gastric carcinoma has strong links to **H. pylori**, atrophic gastritis and intestinal metaplasia. **Lauren classification** splits it into intestinal and diffuse types. The intestinal type is more common in older men and the distal stomach. The diffuse type, with poor gland formation, is more common in young women and the fundus, and includes **linitis plastica**, the leathery stomach. Krukenberg tumour is an ovarian metastasis from a gastric primary.

steps.tx: Staging and surgery follow a clear sequence. Endoscopy with biopsy is the diagnostic test, and EUS is best for local depth. Early gastric cancer is limited to the mucosa and submucosa. A **D2 gastrectomy** removes level 1 and level 2 nodes and is the preferred curative operation. **Virchow node**, the left supraclavicular node, marks spread. Vitamin B12 deficiency can follow gastric cancer or gastrectomy.
